description: Signing in with the Indian international format "+91 90000 00003" fails with "Account not found" for an ACTIVE account (mapped defect auth #13, confirmed live: POST /api/auth/login -> 404).
expected: The +91 / 91 country code is stripped (or matched against the stored 10-digit number), so the receptionist signs in.
actual: Red alert "Account not found (Reference: 7df4b31e-…)". The user is told her account does not exist.
suggested_fix: Normalise identifiers: strip non-digits, then if 12 digits starting with 91 also try the last 10 digits (or store E.164 consistently).

description: Login errors are raw backend strings plus a request UUID: "ThrottlerException: Too Many Requests (Reference: d6c8ecfe-…)", "Invalid password (Reference: 24b42305-…)". The UUID wraps the alert onto two lines.
expected: Plain copy, e.g. "Too many sign-in attempts. Wait a minute and try again." Reference IDs hidden or shown small on a separate line.
actual: Exception class name and a 36-char UUID shown verbatim in the red alert.
suggested_fix: Map known status codes (401/403/404/429) to friendly copy on the login page; render the reference in a muted <small>.

description: Unknown identifier returns "Account not found" (404) while a known one returns "Invalid password" (401), so anyone can probe which phones/emails are staff accounts (mapped defect auth #14, confirmed).
expected: One message for both cases, e.g. "Phone/email or password is incorrect".
actual: riya@clinic.test -> "Account not found"; 9000000003 + wrong password -> "Invalid password".
suggested_fix: Return a single 401 with a generic message for both cases.

description: The login throttle (5/min) is keyed per client IP, not per account. While walking, other sessions from the same machine used up the budget and Riya got "ThrottlerException: Too Many Requests" on her very first attempt. A clinic behind one NAT shares one budget across the whole front desk at opening time.
expected: Throttle per identifier (plus a looser per-IP cap), and say how long to wait.
actual: First attempt of the session rejected with 429.
suggested_fix: Use a ThrottlerGuard tracker keyed on the identifier, or raise the per-IP limit and add a per-account limit.

description: The RECEPTION dashboard leads with admin stat cards: Total Users 10, Active Users 10 (always equal), Total Branches 1, System Status "operational", and a System Alerts panel whose only entry is a hard-coded "System Status — All systems operational / LOW". None of it helps the front desk (mapped defects auth #8 and #9, confirmed).
expected: Front-desk tiles: today's appointments, walk-ins waiting, check-ins; no admin metrics for non-admin roles.
actual: Four admin cards and a fake alert take the top half of the screen.
suggested_fix: Gate the admin cards behind showAdminControls, drop the synthetic System Status alert, and show the empty state when there are no alerts.

description: The "System Status" value "operational" spills 14px past its text column and touches the trend icon (geometry audit overflowSpills: div.flex.items-center "System Statusoperational" 14px).
expected: Value fits beside the icon, or uses a smaller size or a badge.
suggested_fix: Allow the text column to shrink (min-w-0) and truncate, or render status as a badge.

description: At 390px the whole header is hidden: no global search, notifications bell, Branded switch or "Start Tour" (mapped defect auth #15, confirmed). The admin stat cards stack at about 155px each for one number, so Today's Appointments is several screens down.
expected: A compact mobile header with search and bell; compact stat tiles.
actual: Only a hamburger and "ClinicMS" on top; four tall cards before any useful content.
suggested_fix: Render a mobile header row (search icon opening a sheet, bell) and use a 2-column compact stat grid on small screens.

description: The Password placeholder is "••••••••" in medium grey, so an empty field looks pre-filled with a saved password (step 1 shows dots while Sign in is disabled).
expected: An empty-looking field or a text placeholder such as "Password".
suggested_fix: Remove the placeholder or use text.

description: An already signed-in user who opens /login sees the login form again. There is no redirect to /dashboard and no "You are signed in as Riya" hint.
actual: Login form shown with a valid auth_token cookie present.
suggested_fix: In middleware, redirect /login to /dashboard when the auth_token cookie is present (validate on the client).
